rich_narrative.summary: The Intercept is an investigative journalism outlet founded in 2014 that focuses on institutional accountability and civic transparency <cite id="3">through independent news reporting</cite>. Financial data shows <cite id="2">Total Revenue reached $18,961,623 in FY2023</cite>, but experienced a sharp drop to <cite id="2">$5,597,043 in FY2024</cite>. The organization maintained a moderate <cite id="2">program expense ratio of 69.8% in FY2024</cite>, directing funds toward its core investigative newsroom, podcasts, and documentary initiatives. However, overall operations face severe financial headwinds as spending significantly exceeds annual revenue, making ongoing operations dependent on existing reserves. Executive leadership is overseen by CEO Annie Chabel, with total officer compensation recorded at <cite id="2">$1,973,819 in FY2023</cite>. Grantmaking activity includes distributing <cite id="2">$280,000 in domestic grants</cite> to media partners such as Drop Site News Inc.
